# JD+-Quickstart {.unnumbered #quickstart}

The sections below will briefly describe the steps involved in installing JDemetra+, uploading the data, perform seasonal adjustment using the graphical user interface (GUI) of JDemetra+ version 3 and export the data. The guide is intended for a novice user, hence it does not dwell on the theoretical aspects of seasonal adjustment. 

-   How to install JDemetra+

-   How to get data into JDemetra+

-   How to do seasonally adjust your data

-   How to export the data

## JDemetra+ installation
This section will guide the reader through the installation process for the graphical user interface (GUI) and how to configure r to run the rjd3 packages. 

**Graphical User Interface (GUI)**

Before downloading JDemetra+, please be aware that **Version 2.x** of JDemetra (Core, GUI, Cruncher, {RJDemetra}) will be maintained **until December 2026**. This date will also coincide with the end of the official support for Java 8. Please be assured that all existing repositories and files will continue to be accessible beyond December 2026.

You can download the latest releases of JDemetra+ at the following pages:

1. for version 2.x [here](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdemetra-app/releases)
  i) to install [v2.2.4](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdemetra-app/releases/tag/v2.2.4) (this is the latest version of JDemetra+ using Java 8)
    + Scroll down the page, download and unzip the file *jdemetra-2.2.4-bin.zip*.
    + To start the application, run the file **nbdemetra64.exe** located in the following subfolder *...\jdemetra-2.2.4-bin\nbdemetra\bin* 

For easier access, feel free to create shortcuts on your Desktop or in other folders to launch the file.

2. for version 3.x [here](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main/releases)
You should install the latest available release which is denoted v3.x.y
  + Scroll down the page, download and unzip the file *jdemetra-standalone-3.x.y-windows-x86_64.zip*, if you are a Windows user, otherwise, unzip the corresponding file on the OS list.
  + To start the application, run the file **nbdemetra64.exe** located in the following subfolder *...\jdemetra-standalone-3.x.y-windows-x86_64\nbdemetra\bin* 

Version 3.x requires Java 21 or higher. To make things easier, *jdemetra-standalone-3.x.y-windows-x86_64.zip* includes a **portable version of Java**, so you do not need to install or configure it on your system manually.


**How to configure r to run the rjd3 packages**
To use rjd3 packages in R, you need Java 21 or higher.

For the best experience, we recommend using the Java version bundled with the Graphical User Interface (GUI). 
You can download it [here](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main/releases) by following these steps:
  + Navigate the **Assets** section
  + If the file is hidden, click to expand the section.
  + Locate and download the file named **jdemetra-standalone-3.x.y-windows-x86_64.zip**
Once unzipped, the Java file will be located in *C:\Software\jdemetra-standalone-3.x.y-windows-x86_64\nbdemetra\jdk-21.0.2+13-jre* (this file path should be adapted to your computer/server). This location must be declared in R. 
After unzipping the file:
  + at the beginning of your program, run the following code 
```{r}
Sys.setenv(JAVA_HOME = ".../jdemetra-standalone-3.x.y-windows-x86_64/nbdemetra/jdk-21.0.2+13-jre")
```
or 
  + declare it “permanently” is the Renviron file (where environment variables specific to R are stored), following the steps below:
    - in the R console run
```{r} 
file.edit("~/.Renviron") 
```
    - when the file opens, please add the following line of code 
```{r} 
JAVA_HOME = "C:/Software/jdemetra-standalone-3.x.y-windows-x86_64/nbdemetra/jdk-21.0.2+13-jre" 
```
    - save the file and restart R

Follow R packages installation procedure and run basic examples from the readme files of each package. they are all listed [here](https://github.com/rjdverse?view_as=public)


### The structure of the software
  
When JDemetra+ 3 starts, it opens with two main components: **Workspace** and **Providers**.  
  
- **Providers** are the mechanisms used to bring data into JDemetra+. They include several options, most importantly importing data from spreadsheets (see below), but also from databases and other external sources.  
- The **Workspace** is where all your work is organized and saved: seasonal adjustment specifications, input series, and results.  
  
![**Plain JDemetra+ 3**](All_images/PlainJD3.png)  
  
---  
  
### The Workspace and seasonal adjustment  
  
The Workspace is structured into several sections. For seasonal adjustment, the most relevant part is:  
  
- **Seasonal adjustment → Multi-documents**  
  
A *multi-document* is a collection of seasonal adjustment items (often called **SA items**). Each SA item links:  
  
- one input time series,    
- one seasonal adjustment specification, and    
- the corresponding results (decomposition, diagnostics, seasonally adjusted series, etc.).  
  
This allows you to manage and process many series in a consistent way: for each series you can define, store, and reuse a specification, and then compute the seasonally adjusted results.  
  
![**JD3 with opened Workspace**](All_images/JDopenWS.png)  
  
---  
  
### Choosing the method and editing specifications  
  
Within a multi-document, each SA item can be configured individually.  
  
- By **right-clicking** on an SA item, you can choose the **base specification**, in particular whether the series should be adjusted using:  
  - **Tramo-Seats**, or    
  - **X-13-ARIMA** (X-13).  
  
- By **left-clicking** on an SA item, you open the detailed, method-specific **specification editor** (opens on the right side of the panel). Here you can set:  
  - the **ARIMA model** (automatic or user-defined),  
  - **outlier detection and treatment**,  
  - **calendar effects** (trading day, Easter, etc.),  
  - and the detailed options of the **seasonal adjustment** procedure itself (filters, decomposition options, diagnostics).  
  
These specifications can be saved and reused across series.  
  
![**JD3 with specifications open**](All_images/JDspecification.png)  

### Estimation specification and reference specification

The specification you define for an SA-item is called the estimation specification. At the same time, you can define a reference specification that will be a applied in annual campaigns (the annual evaluation of the specifications and results) as a reference or as the starting point for finding a new optimal parameter constellation. How the specifications are defined will be adapted in one of the next releases of JDemetra+, therefore, we will not go into further details here.

## Default seasonal adjustment

| Method      | Name in GUI   | Details                                                                                                                                              |
|-------------|---------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Tramo-Seats | tramoseats    | Decomposition of the time series based on RegARIMA modelling                                                                                         |
| X-13-ARIMA  | x13           | Combination of RegARIMA modelling for calendar effect and moving average based decomposition (X-11) for the extraction of the seasonal effect        |

Full documentation of the Seats method can be found [here](https://jdemetra-new-documentation.netlify.app/m-x11-decomposition), while all details on X-11 can be found [here](https://jdemetra-new-documentation.netlify.app/m-x11-decomposition).
